rows.text: Where there's a will, there's a slay.
Click a monster on the wheel.
Hand is full. Click an item to throw away.
So you've cleared {n} Dungeons. Better hold on to that loot — you'll need it in the next one.
Victory! You made it out - now time to check out {grandpa|poss} trophy collection back at the Cabin.

rows.text: Hey there, greedy goblin. I'm {nib}. I was just in the middle of enjoying my nap when you had to barge into this dungeon and start swiping loot left n' right!
Well, now you've gone and done it — the monsters are coming to claim their stuff, and you're going to have to defend yourself with that loot or else die in this strange catacomb.
Welcome to the Merry Go' Round of doom — a series of circular catacombs that rotate around this particular spot. Don't ask me why, the architect of this dungeon doesn't like answering questions.
This is a Corridor — there are 8 in total. Monsters will pop into these slots as they line up to clean your clock and take your junk.
rows.dir:
(Highlights single empty slice of dungeon wheel)
(Click 'next' to continue)

rows.text: This is your loot. Looks like you started off with some basic loot for this tutorial, but you'll find lots of fancy weapons and armor out here.

rows.dir:
(Sprite of {nib} comes very close to the player, nearly covering 80% of the screen)
(Click to continue)

rows.text:
...is to get out of the dungeon with as much loot as possible.
...Got it?
rows.dir:
(Comes closer)
(Returns to his original position)
(Click 'Got It' to continue)

rows.text: Okay, let me show you how things work a'ROUND these parts.

rows.dir:
(in very tiny text, in italics parentheses) — (y'know, cause of the round dungeon...)
(Click to continue)

rows.text: You have 6 health (HP). You can never have more than 6. If it reaches 0 at any point, you're dead.
When you complete a Dungeon (clear out this wheel), you will heal back to full HP. Spend your HP wisely.

Alright, that's enough. Let's learn the rest as we go. Click Spin. The wheel picks a monster at random. You don't choose who stops in front of you. I'll show you Moves in a minute — that's how you walk to someone. Until then, Spin is a roll.
Ahh, a crotchety ol' wizard, eh?

rows.text: He looks pretty scary — 5 Attack would nearly kill you in one strike.
rows.where: If the wheel landed on Wizard · continue / atk · Nib line

rows.text: ...but he's also super frail. Most weapons will kill him before he gets to strike.
rows.where: If the wheel landed on Wizard · continue / hp · Nib line

rows.text: Use the Sai. It will kill him and end the fight.

rows.text: This Golem is much harder to kill, so block him.

rows.text: You get three Moves for a dungeon. The feet on the wheel. A Move walks you to the next living monster. It does not Spin.
rows.where: After the fight · continue / (none) · Nib line

rows.text: So far you've lost zero HP in this dungeon, but remember — each time you clear a Dungeon, you heal back to full.
rows.where: If Goblin is still waiting · continue / (none) · Nib line

rows.text: AND you get to keep all of the Loot that you didn't use in this dungeon. Pretty sweet, huh?
rows.where: If Goblin is still waiting · continue / (none) · Nib line

rows.where: If Goblin is still waiting · continue / (none) · Nib line

rows.text: Honestly, I respect it. Those Goblins are super annoying, so here's a tip:
rows.where: If they used The Boot · continue / (none) · Nib line

rows.text: Deeper in, a death pulls the next monster out of the deck, and the loot matches whoever walked in. The monster who uses the last card still pays you. Once the deck is empty, the seat closes and you get no more loot. You live on what you are holding.
rows.where: After the fight · continue / (none) · Nib line

rows.text: Come back. Each dungeon you finish, new monsters and new loot join in. The deeper you go, the stranger they get.
rows.where: After the fight · continue / (none) · Nib line

rows.text: The finer the loot, the fiercer its monster.

rows.text: Over the tannery in {village} lived a small goblin with nobody at all.
Then, one rainy night, somebody knocked.
Delivery for the grandchild of {bartleby} {snatchwick}. Sign here. Or bite here. I hear you're a biter.
Your grandfather, the legendary {lucky_snatchwick}, has died inside {mountain}.
He left you everything. Unfortunately, everything is still in the mountain.
Up {hill}, in {the_grumble|poss} shadow, {nib} walks you home.
Here we are, {hero}. Wipe your feet. He never did.
The Last Will & Considerable Testament of {bartleby} {snatchwick}, Esq.
I, {grandpa_full}, being of sound mind and even sounder luck, do hereby leave EVERYTHING to my grandchild, whom I met only once. You bit me. Good instincts.
Everything is presently inside {mountain}, in the pockets of assorted monsters who picked it up after I fell over. Each piece is engraved with my name. They know it is not theirs.
Bring my things home and set them in the {cabinet}. Only what you are holding when you get out counts. What the mountain keeps, it keeps.
When the Cabinet is full, this cabin and the deed to {hill} are yours. {nib} will stamp it. {nib} loves stamping.
{nib} is to be paid in biscuits. Do not open the left-hand drawer of my desk.

Hey friends — thanks for playtesting my game, {game_title}.
Just a few notes before you jump in.

First. This game is in early prototype mode. The things I most want to hear from your feedback are about what is fun, what is boring, what is confusing, and what things you think I should add to the game.
Second. Be honest and picky! You don't need to consider anyone else's perspective. I just want to hear yours.
And finally, have fun! Break the game, find cool combos, test the limits. And don't be afraid to dream big with your requests.
This is the menu you'll land on.
**Brand New** starts from the beginning, as if you had never played.
**Middle Progress** puts you a few dungeons in, with some items already unlocked.
**Continue** picks up your last playtest save.
**Feedback** opens a note to me. Use it for anything that is not tied to one card.
You can right-click any item or monster in the game and leave feedback. That is useful for bugs, confusion, or balance issues.
For general comments while you play, click **Feedback** in the bottom right, or press **F2**.
This is the F2 screen. Type a note, click Send, and it goes to my game development console. Next time I sit down to work, I will see it and can make the fix or the change.
However — for those who want to give the best kind of feedback, I would love to actually HEAR your experience.

Consider taking your phone, setting it to a voice memo or recorder, and just letting it run while you play. Talk out loud about your thought process, your first impressions, your feedback, anything at all.

Then send me the entire file when you are done, because I can turn that into a much more detailed look at your player experience. If you are interested in doing that, you can email the files to me at nathan.elequin@gmail.com.
So thank you again for playtesting. If you have any questions, you can always reach out to me. Now enjoy!
